De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.

Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.
- Raphielle Johnson

    De’Anthony Melton amassed 16 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.

    Melton was one of four Warriors to make at least four three-pointers in Monday’s blowout victory. With Brandon Williams suffering a hamstring injury in the first quarter, Melton is one Warrior whose minutes may increase if Williams misses time. Currently a player who should be rostered in deep leagues, some managers in 12-team leagues may be willing to roll the dice on Melton in the short term.

    De’Anthony Melton accounted for 21 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and six three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Clippers.

    With Stephen Curry getting the night off, Melton started Sunday’s game and played 28 minutes. Unsurprisingly, the one-time fantasy basketball darling recorded a stat line that reminded folks why he remains a popular deep-league option. Melton’s six three-pointers were the most he’s made in a game since December 9, 2022, when he hit eight as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. With Curry expected to play Monday against the Suns, Melton will head back to the bench.
    - Raphielle Johnson

    De’Anthony Melton produced 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Lakers.

    Golden State’s bench made the difference on Friday, outscoring the Lakers’ bench 50-7. Melton scored 13 of his 16 points in the second quarter, shooting 3-of-4 from beyond the arc. He needed just 21 minutes to record his final stat line, showing why Melton can add value for category-league managers despite coming off the bench. The Warriors play one more game this week, hosting the Clippers on Sunday.
    - Raphielle Johnson

    De’Anthony Melton finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 25 points (8-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and four three-pointers.

    Melton didn’t start Saturday’s game, but Stephen Curry’s and Brandin Podziemski’s absences gave him more opportunities. Melton took advantage, scoring 25 points, the most he’s scored in a game since 27 against the Wizards on March 16. Add in the rebounds, assists and steals, and Saturday night was a good one for fantasy managers who slotted Melton into their lineups.
    - Raphielle Johnson
